source.text: Εἶχε μὲν οὖν ἡ πρώτη δικαιώματα λατρείας τό τε ἅγιον κοσμικόν.

records.literal_gloss: Had indeed then the first regulations of worship and the holy [place] earthly.

en.L: So then, the first [covenant] indeed had regulations of worship and the earthly holy place.
en.B: The first covenant, then, had its own regulations for worship, and a sanctuary belonging to this world.
en.R: The first covenant had rules for worship. It also had a holy place here on earth.

es.L: Así pues, el primer [pacto] ciertamente tenía ordenanzas de culto y el lugar santo terrenal.
es.B: El primer pacto, pues, tenía sus propias ordenanzas para el culto, y un santuario que pertenecía a este mundo.
es.R: El primer pacto tenía reglas para la adoración. También tenía un lugar santo aquí en la tierra.

fr.L: Ainsi donc, la première [alliance] avait, certes, des règles de culte et le lieu saint terrestre.
fr.B: La première alliance avait donc ses propres règles pour le culte, et un sanctuaire qui appartenait à ce monde.
fr.R: La première alliance avait des règles pour le culte. Elle avait aussi un lieu saint ici, sur la terre.

sw.L: Basi, [agano] la kwanza kweli lilikuwa na masharti ya ibada na mahali patakatifu pa kidunia.
sw.B: Basi agano la kwanza lilikuwa na masharti yake ya ibada, na mahali patakatifu palipo katika ulimwengu huu.
sw.R: Agano la kwanza lilikuwa na kanuni za kuabudu. Pia lilikuwa na mahali patakatifu hapa duniani.

decisions.choice: the first: the first covenant
decisions.reason: The feminine πρώτη has no noun. The last sentence of chapter 8 spoke of the first covenant as old and about to disappear (8:13), so the word to supply is "covenant" (διαθήκη), as again in 9:18. Some later manuscripts add the word for "tent" here, but the earliest do not, and the SBLGNT does not; reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: earthly sanctuary: a holy place belonging to this world, set up by human hands
alternatives: a sanctuary for the whole world
decisions.reason: κοσμικόν means "belonging to the world". The author contrasts this sanctuary with the one "not made with hands, that is, not of this creation" (9:11, 9:24). The singular ἅγιον here means the whole sanctuary, both its rooms, which verses 2-5 go on to describe.

decisions.choice: holy place (Literal), sanctuary (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "holy place" for this adjective used as a noun throughout the chapter; Balanced says "sanctuary". It is not the temple: the author describes the tent of the wilderness years (Exodus 25-27).

decisions.choice: pacto (the supplied noun at Literal agrees with it: "el primer [pacto]")
decisions.reason: "Pacto" is the Spanish word for covenant through Hebrews, at every level; only in 9:16-17, where the same Greek word means a last will, does Spanish say "testamento". "Pacto" is masculine, so the Spanish says "el primer" where the Greek feminine πρώτη agrees with the covenant word.

decisions.choice: agano (the supplied noun at Literal agrees with it: "[agano] la kwanza")
decisions.reason: "Agano" is the Swahili word for covenant through Hebrews, at every level; only in 9:16-17, where the same Greek word means a last will, does Swahili say "wasia". The adjective "la kwanza" takes the agreement of "agano", so Literal supplies that noun in brackets.

decisions.choice: alliance (the supplied noun at Literal agrees with it: "la première [alliance]")
decisions.reason: "Alliance" is the French word for covenant through Hebrews, at every level; only in 9:16-17, where the same Greek word means a last will, does French say "testament". "Alliance" is feminine, like the Greek word, so "la première" agrees with it as the Greek feminine does.

source.text: σκηνὴ γὰρ κατεσκευάσθη ἡ πρώτη ἐν ᾗ ἥ τε λυχνία καὶ ἡ τράπεζα καὶ ἡ πρόθεσις τῶν ἄρτων, ἥτις λέγεται Ἅγια·

records.literal_gloss: A tent for was prepared, the first, in which [were] both the lampstand and the table and the presentation of the loaves, which is called Holy [Place];

en.L: For a tent was prepared, the first, in which [were] the lampstand and the table and the presentation of the loaves, which is called [the] Holy Place.
en.B: A first tabernacle was set up, which held the lampstand, and the table with the loaves set out on it. This one is called the Holy Place.
en.R: A sacred tent was set up. Its outer room held the lampstand and the table with the special bread set out before God. This room was called the Holy Place.

es.L: Porque fue preparada una tienda, la primera, en la cual [estaban] el candelabro y la mesa y la presentación de los panes, la cual se llama [el] Lugar Santo.
es.B: Se dispuso un primer tabernáculo, que contenía el candelabro y la mesa con los panes colocados sobre ella. Este se llama el Lugar Santo.
es.R: Se levantó una tienda sagrada. Su sala exterior tenía el candelabro y la mesa con el pan especial puesto delante de Dios. Esta sala se llamaba el Lugar Santo.

fr.L: Car une tente fut aménagée, la première, dans laquelle [se trouvaient] le chandelier, la table et la présentation des pains, laquelle est appelée [le] Lieu saint.
fr.B: Un premier tabernacle fut dressé, où se trouvaient le chandelier, et la table avec les pains qu’on y exposait. On l’appelle le Lieu saint.
fr.R: On a dressé une tente sacrée. Sa pièce extérieure contenait le chandelier, et la table où l’on plaçait un pain spécial devant Dieu. Cette pièce s’appelait le Lieu saint.

sw.L: Kwa maana hema iliandaliwa, ile ya kwanza, ambamo [mlikuwa na] kinara cha taa na meza na uwekaji wa mikate, ambayo inaitwa Patakatifu.
sw.B: Hema ya kwanza ilisimamishwa, ambamo mlikuwa na kinara cha taa, na meza yenye mikate iliyopangwa juu yake. Hema hii inaitwa Patakatifu.
sw.R: Hema takatifu ilijengwa. Chumba chake cha nje kilikuwa na kinara cha taa na meza yenye mikate maalum iliyowekwa mbele za Mungu. Chumba hiki kiliitwa Patakatifu.

decisions.choice: the first tent: the outer room of the tabernacle, which the author treats as a tent of its own
alternatives: the earlier tabernacle as a whole
decisions.reason: Exodus describes one tent divided by a curtain into two rooms (Exodus 26:33). The author speaks of them as a first tent (verses 2, 6) and a second (verses 3, 7), the outer room being the one a priest enters first.

decisions.choice: the lampstand, the table and the bread set out on it: the furnishings of the outer room
decisions.reason: The golden lampstand (Exodus 25:31-40) and the table (Exodus 25:23-30) stood in the outer room. Twelve loaves were laid out on the table before the LORD every Sabbath (Leviticus 24:5-9; Exodus 25:30); πρόθεσις τῶν ἄρτων names this setting out of the bread.

decisions.choice: tent (Literal), tabernacle (Balanced), sacred tent (Readable)
decisions.reason: σκηνὴ is the ordinary word for a tent. Literal says "tent" so the reader sees the plain word; Balanced uses the familiar name "tabernacle"; Readable says "sacred tent", which needs no church vocabulary. These are used throughout Hebrews.

decisions.choice: its outer room
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the "first tent" is the outer room of the one tent, so that the next verse's "second" tent is understood as the inner room.

decisions.choice: the special bread set out before God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the bread was: loaves set out before God (Exodus 25:30).

decisions.choice: tienda (Literal), tabernáculo (Balanced), tienda sagrada (Readable)
decisions.reason: As the English does with tent, tabernacle and sacred tent: Literal keeps the plain word for a tent, Balanced the familiar name of the wilderness sanctuary, and Readable says what kind of tent it was. Spanish "tienda" is feminine and "tabernáculo" masculine, so "la primera tienda" (Literal) becomes "el primer tabernáculo" (Balanced).

decisions.choice: hema (Literal, Balanced), hema takatifu (Readable)
decisions.reason: Swahili has no separate church word for the tabernacle in common use, so Literal and Balanced both say "hema", the plain word for a tent that the Greek uses. Readable says "hema takatifu", as the English Readable says "sacred tent".

decisions.choice: la présentation des pains (Literal), les pains qu’on y exposait (Balanced)
decisions.reason: "Pains de proposition" is the traditional French name, but "proposition" no longer means "setting out" to a modern reader. Literal keeps the Greek noun as "la présentation des pains"; Balanced says what was done with the bread; Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

source.text: μετὰ δὲ τὸ δεύτερον καταπέτασμα σκηνὴ ἡ λεγομένη Ἅγια Ἁγίων, χρυσοῦν ἔχουσα θυμιατήριον καὶ τὴν κιβωτὸν τῆς διαθήκης περικεκαλυμμένην πάντοθεν χρυσίῳ, ἐν ᾗ στάμνος χρυσῆ ἔχουσα τὸ μάννα καὶ ἡ ῥάβδος Ἀαρὼν ἡ βλαστήσασα καὶ αἱ πλάκες τῆς διαθήκης, ὑπεράνω δὲ αὐτῆς Χερουβὶν δόξης κατασκιάζοντα τὸ ἱλαστήριον· περὶ ὧν οὐκ ἔστιν νῦν λέγειν κατὰ μέρος.

records.literal_gloss: After now the second curtain, a tent the [one] being called Holy of Holies, \v 4 golden having altar of incense and the ark of the covenant covered around on all sides with gold, in which [was] a jar golden having the manna and the staff of Aaron the [one] having budded and the tablets of the covenant, \v 5 above and it cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat; concerning which not it is now to speak in detail.

en.L: And behind the second curtain [was] a tent called [the] Holy of Holies, \v 4 having a golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant covered on all sides with gold, in which [were] a golden jar holding the manna and the staff of Aaron that budded and the tablets of the covenant, \v 5 and above it cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat. Concerning these things it is not now [the time] to speak in detail.
en.B: Beyond the second curtain stood a tabernacle called the Most Holy Place. \v 4 To it belonged the golden altar of incense, and in it was the ark of the covenant, overlaid with gold on every side. The ark held a golden jar containing the manna, the staff of Aaron that sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant. \v 5 Over the ark the cherubim of glory spread their shadow across the mercy seat. Of these things there is no time now to speak one by one.
en.R: Behind the second curtain was the inner room, called the Most Holy Place. \v 4 The golden altar for burning incense belonged to this room. In it was the ark of the covenant, a chest covered with gold on every side. Inside the ark were a gold jar with manna in it, the staff of Aaron that had grown buds, and the tablets of the covenant. \v 5 On top of the ark were the cherubim, winged figures that showed God's glory was there. Their wings spread over the mercy seat. This was the lid of the ark, where atonement was made. But now is not the time to explain all these things one by one.

es.L: Y tras la segunda cortina [había] una tienda llamada [el] Santo de los Santos, \v 4 que tenía un altar de oro para el incienso y el arca del pacto cubierta de oro por todos lados, en la cual [había] una vasija de oro que contenía el maná, y la vara de Aarón que retoñó, y las tablas del pacto; \v 5 y sobre ella, querubines de gloria que cubrían con su sombra el propiciatorio. Acerca de estas cosas no es [el momento] ahora de hablar en detalle.
es.B: Detrás de la segunda cortina había un tabernáculo llamado el Lugar Santísimo. \v 4 A él pertenecía el altar de oro del incienso, y en él estaba el arca del pacto, recubierta de oro por todos lados. El arca contenía una vasija de oro con el maná, la vara de Aarón que había retoñado y las tablas del pacto. \v 5 Sobre el arca, los querubines de la gloria extendían su sombra sobre el propiciatorio. De estas cosas no hay tiempo ahora para hablar una por una.
es.R: Detrás de la segunda cortina estaba la sala interior, llamada el Lugar Santísimo. \v 4 El altar de oro para quemar incienso pertenecía a esta sala. En ella estaba el arca del pacto, un cofre cubierto de oro por todos lados. Dentro del arca había una vasija de oro con maná, la vara de Aarón a la que le habían salido brotes, y las tablas del pacto. \v 5 Encima del arca estaban los querubines, figuras con alas que mostraban que la gloria de Dios estaba allí. Sus alas se extendían sobre el propiciatorio. Esta era la tapa del arca, donde se hacía la expiación. Pero ahora no es el momento de explicar todas estas cosas una por una.

fr.L: Et derrière le second rideau [se trouvait] une tente appelée [le] Saint des Saints, \v 4 ayant un autel d’or pour l’encens et l’arche de l’alliance couverte d’or de tous côtés, dans laquelle [étaient] une jarre d’or contenant la manne, le bâton d’Aaron qui avait bourgeonné et les tables de l’alliance, \v 5 et au-dessus d’elle des chérubins de gloire couvrant de leur ombre le propitiatoire. De ces choses, ce n’est pas maintenant [le moment] de parler en détail.
fr.B: Derrière le second rideau se trouvait un tabernacle appelé le Lieu très saint. \v 4 Il avait l’autel d’or pour l’encens, et il renfermait l’arche de l’alliance, revêtue d’or de toutes parts. L’arche contenait une jarre d’or où était la manne, le bâton d’Aaron qui avait bourgeonné, et les tables de l’alliance. \v 5 Au-dessus de l’arche, les chérubins de la gloire étendaient leur ombre sur le propitiatoire. Ce n’est pas le moment d’en parler maintenant point par point.
fr.R: Derrière le second rideau se trouvait la pièce intérieure, appelée le Lieu très saint. \v 4 L’autel d’or où l’on brûlait l’encens faisait partie de cette pièce. On y trouvait l’arche de l’alliance, un coffre couvert d’or de tous les côtés. Dans l’arche, il y avait une jarre d’or avec de la manne, le bâton d’Aaron qui avait fait des bourgeons, et les tables de l’alliance. \v 5 Sur l’arche se trouvaient les chérubins, des figures ailées qui montraient que la gloire de Dieu était là. Leurs ailes s’étendaient au-dessus du propitiatoire. C’était le couvercle de l’arche, où l’on faisait l’expiation des péchés. Mais ce n’est pas le moment d’expliquer toutes ces choses une par une.

sw.L: Na nyuma ya pazia la pili [kulikuwa na] hema iitwayo Patakatifu pa Patakatifu, \v 4 yenye madhabahu ya dhahabu ya uvumba na sanduku la agano lililofunikwa pande zote kwa dhahabu, ambamo [mlikuwa na] chungu cha dhahabu chenye mana, na fimbo ya Haruni iliyochipuka, na mabamba ya agano, \v 5 na juu yake makerubi ya utukufu yakitia kivuli kiti cha rehema. Kuhusu mambo hayo si sasa [wakati] wa kusema kila kimoja kwa undani.
sw.B: Nyuma ya pazia la pili ilikuwapo hema iitwayo Patakatifu pa Patakatifu. \v 4 Ilikuwa na madhabahu ya dhahabu ya kufukizia uvumba, na ndani yake lilikuwa sanduku la agano, lililofunikwa kwa dhahabu kila upande. Ndani ya sanduku hilo mlikuwa na chungu cha dhahabu chenye mana, fimbo ya Haruni iliyochipua, na mabamba ya agano. \v 5 Juu ya sanduku makerubi ya utukufu yalitandaza kivuli chao juu ya kiti cha rehema. Hatuna nafasi sasa ya kueleza mambo haya moja moja.
sw.R: Nyuma ya pazia la pili kulikuwa na chumba cha ndani, kilichoitwa Patakatifu pa Patakatifu. \v 4 Madhabahu ya dhahabu ya kufukizia uvumba ilikuwa ya chumba hiki. Ndani yake kulikuwa na sanduku la agano, kasha lililofunikwa kwa dhahabu kila upande. Ndani ya sanduku hilo kulikuwa na chungu cha dhahabu chenye mana, fimbo ya Haruni iliyokuwa imechipua, na mabamba ya agano. \v 5 Juu ya sanduku kulikuwa na makerubi, maumbo ya viumbe wenye mabawa yaliyoonyesha kwamba utukufu wa Mungu ulikuwa pale. Mabawa yao yalitanda juu ya kiti cha rehema. Hicho kilikuwa kifuniko cha sanduku, mahali ambapo upatanisho ulifanyika. Lakini sasa si wakati wa kueleza mambo haya yote moja moja.

decisions.choice: the second curtain: the veil between the outer room and the inner room
decisions.reason: The tabernacle had a screen at its entrance (Exodus 26:36) and a veil inside dividing the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place (Exodus 26:31-33). The second curtain is that inner veil.

decisions.choice: a golden altar of incense
alternatives: a golden censer (a pan for carrying burning coals and incense)
decisions.reason: θυμιατήριον means a thing for burning incense. In the Greek Old Testament it can mean a censer (2 Chronicles 26:19; Ezekiel 8:11), and on the Day of Atonement the high priest carried burning coals and incense inside the veil (Leviticus 16:12-13), but Exodus never mentions a golden censer kept in the inner room. Jewish writers of the period who wrote in Greek use the word for the golden altar of incense (Exodus 30:1-10), the one major piece of gold furniture the list would otherwise leave out. Against this, that altar stood in front of the veil, not behind it (Exodus 30:6; 40:26). The evidence is divided.

decisions.choice: having: belonging to the Most Holy Place by its use, not necessarily standing inside it
alternatives: standing inside the Most Holy Place
decisions.reason: The author says the inner tent "has" the altar, not that the altar was "in" it, as he does say of the jar and staff ("in which"). The incense altar stood "before the veil that is over the ark" (Exodus 30:6), its incense rose before the mercy seat, and its horns were smeared with the atonement blood (Exodus 30:10; Leviticus 16:18). 1 Kings 6:22 likewise calls the temple's altar the one that belonged to the inner sanctuary.

decisions.choice: in which: inside the ark were the jar of manna, Aaron's staff and the tablets
decisions.reason: Exodus 16:33-34 and Numbers 17:10 say the jar of manna and Aaron's staff were put "before the testimony", that is, before the ark; Deuteronomy 10:2-5 puts the tablets inside it. 1 Kings 8:9 says that in Solomon's day only the tablets were in the ark. The author follows the tradition that all three were kept in it, in the wilderness tabernacle he is describing.

decisions.choice: the staff of Aaron that budded: the sign that God had chosen Aaron's family for the priesthood
decisions.reason: In Numbers 17:1-11 the staffs of the twelve tribes were left before the LORD overnight, and Aaron's sprouted, blossomed and bore almonds. It was kept as a sign against rebellion. The detail fits the author's theme of who is called to be high priest (5:4).

decisions.choice: cherubim of glory: the winged figures over the ark, linked with God's glorious presence
alternatives: glorious cherubim (only a description of their splendor)
decisions.reason: Two gold cherubim faced each other over the ark with wings spread (Exodus 25:18-22). God promised to meet Moses there, "from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim" (Exodus 25:22), and his glory filled the tabernacle (Exodus 40:34). "Of glory" points to that presence.

decisions.choice: mercy seat: the gold lid of the ark, where the blood of atonement was sprinkled
decisions.reason: ἱλαστήριον is the word the Greek Old Testament uses for the gold cover of the ark (Exodus 25:17-22). On the Day of Atonement the high priest sprinkled blood on it and before it (Leviticus 16:14-15). Paul uses the same word of Christ in Romans 3:25.

decisions.choice: mercy seat
decisions.reason: "Mercy seat" is the long-established English name for the ark's cover and is kept at Literal and Balanced; Readable adds what it was.

decisions.choice: the mercy seat. This was the lid of the ark, where atonement was made.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the term in a short added sentence, as the meaning decision describes it.

decisions.choice: Holy of Holies (Literal), Most Holy Place (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew-style phrase "holy of holies", which means the holiest place. Balanced and Readable say it in plain English, as "the Holy Place" is said in verse 2.

decisions.choice: the cherubim, winged figures that showed God's glory was there
decisions.reason: Readable explains what cherubim were and what "of glory" means here.

decisions.choice: the golden altar for burning incense
decisions.reason: Readable follows the meaning decision and says what the altar was for. The footnote gives the other possible sense.

decisions.choice: Santo de los Santos (Literal), Lugar Santísimo (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew-style phrase "holy of holies" that the Greek reproduces; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary Spanish name for the inner room, as the English uses Most Holy Place.

decisions.choice: cortina; propiciatorio
decisions.reason: "Cortina" follows the English "curtain" and says plainly what hung there; "velo" is the older church word. "Propiciatorio" is the established Spanish name for the lid of the ark; Readable explains it in a following sentence, as the English does for mercy seat.

decisions.choice: Patakatifu pa Patakatifu (every level)
alternatives: Patakatifu pa Patakatifu (Literal) and a plainer name elsewhere
decisions.reason: The Swahili name for the inner room already follows the Hebrew-style phrase word for word and is the ordinary name for it, so one form serves all three levels where the English has "Holy of Holies" and "Most Holy Place".

decisions.choice: pazia; kiti cha rehema
decisions.reason: "Pazia" is the word settled for the curtain through Hebrews. "Kiti cha rehema" is the established Swahili name for the lid of the ark and matches the English "mercy seat"; Readable explains it in an added sentence, as the English does.

decisions.choice: propitiatoire
decisions.reason: "Propitiatoire" is the established French name for the ark's cover, as "mercy seat" is in English, and it keeps the link with the same Greek word in Romans 3:25. It is a learned word, so Readable keeps it and adds a short sentence saying what it was, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: rideau
decisions.reason: "Voile" is the traditional French word for the curtain of the sanctuary, but to a modern reader it suggests a thin fabric or a head covering. "Rideau" names a hanging that closes off a room, and it is used for this Greek word through Hebrews (6:19; 10:20).

source.text: Τούτων δὲ οὕτως κατεσκευασμένων, εἰς μὲν τὴν πρώτην σκηνὴν διὰ παντὸς εἰσίασιν οἱ ἱερεῖς τὰς λατρείας ἐπιτελοῦντες, εἰς δὲ τὴν δευτέραν ἅπαξ τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ μόνος ὁ ἀρχιερεύς, οὐ χωρὶς αἵματος, ὃ προσφέρει ὑπὲρ ἑαυτοῦ καὶ τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ ἀγνοημάτων, τοῦτο δηλοῦντος τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου, μήπω πεφανερῶσθαι τὴν τῶν ἁγίων ὁδὸν ἔτι τῆς πρώτης σκηνῆς ἐχούσης στάσιν, ἥτις παραβολὴ εἰς τὸν καιρὸν τὸν ἐνεστηκότα, καθ’ ἣν δῶρά τε καὶ θυσίαι προσφέρονται μὴ δυνάμεναι κατὰ συνείδησιν τελειῶσαι τὸν λατρεύοντα, μόνον ἐπὶ βρώμασιν καὶ πόμασιν καὶ διαφόροις βαπτισμοῖς, δικαιώματα σαρκὸς μέχρι καιροῦ διορθώσεως ἐπικείμενα.

records.literal_gloss: These things now thus having been prepared, into indeed the first tent through all [time] enter the priests the services accomplishing, \v 7 into but the second once of the year alone the high priest, not without blood, which he offers for himself and the of the people sins of ignorance, \v 8 this making clear the Spirit the Holy, not yet to have been made manifest the of the holy [place] way, still the first tent having standing, \v 9 which [is] a parable for the time the present, according to which gifts both and sacrifices are offered not being able as to conscience to make perfect the [one] worshiping, \v 10 only on foods and drinks and various washings, regulations of flesh until a time of setting right being imposed.

en.L: Now these things having been thus prepared, the priests enter the first tent continually, performing the services, \v 7 but into the second only the high priest [enters], once a year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the sins of ignorance of the people, \v 8 the Holy Spirit making this clear, that the way [into] the holy place has not yet been made manifest while the first tent still has standing, \v 9 which [is] a parable for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that are not able to make perfect with respect to conscience the one worshiping, \v 10 [resting] only on foods and drinks and various washings, regulations of [the] flesh imposed until a time of setting [things] right.
en.B: With these things arranged in this way, the priests go regularly into the first tabernacle as they carry out their duties of worship. \v 7 But into the second the high priest goes alone, once a year, and he must bring blood, which he offers for his own sins and for those the people committed without knowing it. \v 8 By this the Holy Spirit makes it clear that the way into the sanctuary has not yet been opened as long as the first tabernacle still has its place. \v 9 This is a figure for the present time. Under this arrangement gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot make the worshiper perfect in conscience. \v 10 They have to do only with what is eaten and drunk and with various washings, regulations for the body imposed until the time comes to set things right.
en.R: With everything set up like this, the priests go into the outer room of the sacred tent all the time to do their work of worship. \v 7 But only the high priest goes into the inner room, and only once a year, on the Day of Atonement. He always takes blood with him. He offers it for his own sins and for the sins the people have done without knowing it. \v 8 In this way the Holy Spirit shows that the way into God's presence is not yet open as long as the outer room of the tent still has its place. \v 9 This is a picture for the present time. The gifts and sacrifices offered there cannot make worshipers complete in their conscience. \v 10 They deal only with food and drink and different kinds of washing. These are rules for the body, given until the time when God would set things right.

es.L: Y estando estas cosas así preparadas, en la primera tienda entran continuamente los sacerdotes, cumpliendo los servicios del culto; \v 7 pero en la segunda [entra] solo el sumo sacerdote, una vez al año, no sin sangre, la cual ofrece por sí mismo y por los pecados de ignorancia del pueblo; \v 8 dando a entender esto el Espíritu Santo: que todavía no se ha manifestado el camino [hacia] el lugar santo mientras la primera tienda sigue en pie, \v 9 lo cual [es] una parábola para el tiempo presente, según la cual se ofrecen dones y sacrificios que no pueden hacer perfecto en cuanto a la conciencia al que rinde culto, \v 10 [basados] solo en comidas y bebidas y diversos lavamientos, ordenanzas de [la] carne impuestas hasta un tiempo de enderezar [las cosas].
es.B: Dispuestas así estas cosas, los sacerdotes entran con regularidad en el primer tabernáculo para cumplir sus funciones de culto. \v 7 Pero en el segundo entra solo el sumo sacerdote, una vez al año, y tiene que llevar sangre, que ofrece por sus propios pecados y por los que el pueblo cometió sin saberlo. \v 8 Con esto el Espíritu Santo deja claro que el camino al santuario aún no ha sido abierto mientras el primer tabernáculo conserve su lugar. \v 9 Esto es una figura para el tiempo presente. Según este orden se ofrecen dones y sacrificios que no pueden hacer perfecto en su conciencia al que rinde culto. \v 10 Solo tienen que ver con lo que se come y se bebe y con diversos lavamientos, ordenanzas para el cuerpo impuestas hasta que llegue el tiempo de enderezar las cosas.
es.R: Con todo preparado así, los sacerdotes entran todo el tiempo en la sala exterior de la tienda sagrada para hacer su trabajo de adoración. \v 7 Pero en la sala interior entra solo el sumo sacerdote, y solo una vez al año, en el Día de la Expiación. Siempre lleva sangre consigo. La ofrece por sus propios pecados y por los pecados que el pueblo ha cometido sin saberlo. \v 8 De esta manera el Espíritu Santo muestra que el camino a la presencia de Dios todavía no está abierto mientras la sala exterior de la tienda siga teniendo su lugar. \v 9 Esto es una imagen para el tiempo presente. Los dones y sacrificios que se ofrecen allí no pueden hacer que los que adoran queden completos en su conciencia. \v 10 Solo tienen que ver con comida y bebida y con distintas clases de lavamientos. Son reglas para el cuerpo, dadas hasta el tiempo en que Dios pondría las cosas en orden.

fr.L: Or ces choses étant ainsi disposées, les prêtres entrent continuellement dans la première tente, accomplissant le service du culte, \v 7 mais dans la seconde, le grand prêtre seul [entre], une fois par an, non sans sang, qu’il offre pour lui-même et pour les péchés d’ignorance du peuple, \v 8 l’Esprit Saint montrant ceci : le chemin du lieu saint n’a pas encore été manifesté tant que la première tente est encore debout, \v 9 laquelle [est] une parabole pour le temps présent, selon laquelle sont offerts des dons et des sacrifices qui ne peuvent pas rendre parfait, quant à la conscience, celui qui rend le culte, \v 10 [reposant] seulement sur des aliments, des boissons et diverses ablutions, règles de [la] chair imposées jusqu’à un temps de redressement.
fr.B: Ces choses étant ainsi disposées, les prêtres entrent régulièrement dans le premier tabernacle pour accomplir leur service du culte. \v 7 Mais dans le second, le grand prêtre entre seul, une fois par an, et il doit apporter du sang, qu’il offre pour ses propres péchés et pour ceux que le peuple a commis sans le savoir. \v 8 L’Esprit Saint montre ainsi que le chemin du sanctuaire n’est pas encore ouvert tant que le premier tabernacle a encore sa place. \v 9 C’est là une figure pour le temps présent. Dans ce système, on offre des dons et des sacrifices qui ne peuvent pas rendre parfait dans sa conscience celui qui rend le culte. \v 10 Ils ne concernent que ce qu’on mange et ce qu’on boit, et diverses ablutions : ce sont des règles pour le corps, imposées jusqu’au temps où tout serait remis en ordre.
fr.R: Quand tout a été installé ainsi, les prêtres entrent tout le temps dans la pièce extérieure de la tente sacrée pour faire leur travail de culte. \v 7 Mais seul le grand prêtre entre dans la pièce intérieure, et seulement une fois par an, le jour du Grand Pardon. Il apporte toujours du sang avec lui. Il l’offre pour ses propres péchés et pour les péchés que le peuple a commis sans le savoir. \v 8 De cette manière, l’Esprit Saint montre que le chemin vers la présence de Dieu n’est pas encore ouvert tant que la pièce extérieure de la tente a encore sa place. \v 9 C’est une image pour le temps présent. Les dons et les sacrifices qu’on offre là ne peuvent pas rendre complets dans leur conscience ceux qui rendent le culte. \v 10 Ils concernent seulement la nourriture, la boisson et différentes sortes de lavages. Ce sont des règles pour le corps, données jusqu’au moment où Dieu remettrait tout en ordre.

sw.L: Basi mambo haya yakiisha kuandaliwa hivyo, makuhani huingia daima katika hema ya kwanza wakitimiza huduma za ibada, \v 7 lakini katika ile ya pili kuhani mkuu peke yake [huingia], mara moja kwa mwaka, si bila damu, anayoitoa kwa ajili yake mwenyewe na kwa ajili ya dhambi za watu za kutojua, \v 8 Roho Mtakatifu akionyesha wazi hili, kwamba njia ya [kuingia] mahali patakatifu bado haijadhihirishwa wakati hema ya kwanza ingali imesimama, \v 9 ambayo [ni] mfano kwa wakati uliopo, ambao kwa mujibu wake matoleo na dhabihu hutolewa visivyoweza kumkamilisha kwa upande wa dhamiri yule anayeabudu, \v 10 [vikihusu] vyakula na vinywaji tu na kuosha kwa namna mbalimbali, masharti ya mwili yaliyowekwa hadi wakati wa kunyoosha [mambo].
sw.B: Mambo haya yakiwa yamepangwa hivyo, makuhani huingia mara kwa mara katika hema ya kwanza wakitekeleza kazi zao za ibada. \v 7 Lakini katika hema ya pili huingia kuhani mkuu peke yake, mara moja kwa mwaka, naye lazima aingie na damu, anayoitoa kwa ajili ya dhambi zake mwenyewe na kwa ajili ya dhambi ambazo watu walizitenda bila kujua. \v 8 Kwa jambo hili Roho Mtakatifu anaonyesha wazi kwamba njia ya kuingia mahali patakatifu haijafunguliwa bado, maadamu hema ya kwanza ingali na nafasi yake. \v 9 Jambo hilo ni kielelezo kwa wakati huu wa sasa. Kwa mpango huo matoleo na dhabihu hutolewa ambavyo haviwezi kumkamilisha mwabudu katika dhamiri yake. \v 10 Vinahusu tu vyakula na vinywaji na kuosha kwa namna mbalimbali, masharti ya mwili yaliyowekwa hadi utakapofika wakati wa kuyanyoosha mambo.
sw.R: Kila kitu kikiwa kimepangwa hivyo, makuhani huingia katika chumba cha nje cha hema takatifu wakati wote ili kufanya kazi yao ya ibada. \v 7 Lakini ni kuhani mkuu peke yake anayeingia katika chumba cha ndani, tena mara moja tu kwa mwaka, katika Siku ya Upatanisho. Kila mara huingia na damu. Huitoa kwa ajili ya dhambi zake mwenyewe na kwa ajili ya dhambi ambazo watu wamezitenda bila kujua. \v 8 Kwa njia hii Roho Mtakatifu anaonyesha kwamba njia ya kuingia mbele za Mungu bado haijafunguliwa, maadamu chumba cha nje cha hema kingali na nafasi yake. \v 9 Hii ni picha kwa wakati huu wa sasa. Matoleo na dhabihu vinavyotolewa huko haviwezi kuwakamilisha wanaoabudu katika dhamiri zao. \v 10 Vinahusu vyakula na vinywaji tu, na namna mbalimbali za kuosha. Hizo ni kanuni za mwili, zilizotolewa hadi wakati ambapo Mungu angeyaweka mambo sawa.

decisions.choice: once a year, the high priest alone, with blood: the Day of Atonement
decisions.reason: Leviticus 16 describes the one day each year when the high priest alone went behind the veil (Leviticus 16:2, 16:29-34). He took the blood of a bull for himself and his household and the blood of a goat for the people, and sprinkled it on and before the mercy seat (Leviticus 16:11-15). The author's "not without blood" sums up that rite. Day by day the other priests tended the lamps and burned incense in the outer room (Exodus 27:21; 30:7-8).

decisions.choice: sins of ignorance: wrongs done without knowing or intending them
decisions.reason: ἀγνοημάτων means a sin done in ignorance. The law provided sacrifices for unintentional sins (Leviticus 4:2; Numbers 15:22-29), and the Day of Atonement covered all the people's sins (Leviticus 16:16, 16:21). The author's word stresses human weakness, as in 5:2, where the high priest deals gently with those who sin in ignorance.

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit making this clear: the Spirit teaches through the way the tabernacle was ordered
alternatives: the author's own inference, credited loosely to the Spirit
decisions.reason: Hebrews hears the Holy Spirit speaking in Scripture (3:7; 10:15). Here the Spirit shows something through the layout and rites of the tabernacle that Scripture records: the inner room was closed to all but one man, one day a year.

decisions.choice: the way into the holy place: access into God's presence, of which the inner room was a copy
alternatives: the way into the earthly inner room only
decisions.reason: ἁγίων is the plural the author uses for the sanctuary, both earthly (9:25) and heavenly (9:12, 9:24; 10:19). The point is that while the earthly arrangement lasted, ordinary worshipers had no way in to God; Christ has now opened it (10:19-20).

decisions.choice: while the first tent still has standing: while the outer room, and the whole earthly order of worship it stands for, still has its place
alternatives: while the earlier (Mosaic) tabernacle as a whole still stands
while the outer room still physically stands
decisions.reason: In verses 2 and 6 "the first tent" is the outer room, and that is the natural sense here. But the outer room is also the part the people's priests served in, so it stands for the whole earthly system of worship, which the author has called the first covenant (8:13). στάσιν means standing or status, not only a building being upright. The two senses overlap and cannot be cleanly separated.

decisions.choice: a parable for the present time: the outer tent is an illustration whose meaning bears on the time now present, while the old offerings still go on
alternatives: a symbol of the age then present, the old order now past
a symbol pointing to the new age that has now arrived
decisions.reason: παραβολὴ means a comparison or illustration (in the Gospels, a parable). "The present time" could be the time then present under the old order, or the time of the author and readers, in which the gifts and sacrifices "are offered" (present tense) and which lasts until "the time of setting things right" (verse 10). The author likely means the present time, in which the old rites still go on but are already shown to be temporary. The other readings are close in sense and both have support.

decisions.choice: according to which: under this arrangement, the order the illustration points to
decisions.reason: The feminine relative ἣν most likely looks back to the "parable" (παραβολὴ), the arrangement just described; it cannot refer to "time", which is masculine.

decisions.choice: make the worshiper perfect in conscience: bring worshipers to the goal of a clean conscience and free access to God (as at 2:10)
decisions.reason: τελειόω means to bring to the goal or completion. Here the goal is inward: a conscience cleansed so that the worshiper can approach God (9:14; 10:1-2, 10:22). The sacrifices could deal with outward impurity but not with this.

decisions.choice: washings: ritual washings for purity
decisions.reason: βαπτισμοῖς here means the many ritual washings of the law (Leviticus 11-15; Numbers 19), not Christian baptism. The same word in 6:2 is also plural.

decisions.choice: regulations of the flesh: the gifts, sacrifices and food and washing rules are outward rules for the body, imposed for a limited time
alternatives: regulations that belong to sinful human nature
decisions.reason: δικαιώματα stands in apposition to the gifts and sacrifices of verse 9. σαρκὸς here means the outward, bodily side of life, as in verse 13 ("the cleanness of the flesh"), not the sinful nature. The rules were "imposed" (a burden laid on) until a set time.

decisions.choice: a time of setting things right: the time when God puts in place the new order, the new covenant
alternatives: a time of reform of the old rules
decisions.reason: διορθώσεως means making straight or correcting. The author has just spoken of the new covenant promised in Jeremiah 31:31-34 (8:8-13), and the next verse begins with Christ's coming, so this is the time of the new covenant.

decisions.choice: make complete
decisions.reason: Readable says "make complete" for this verb, since "perfect" suggests moral flawlessness. Literal and Balanced keep "perfect", as through Hebrews.

decisions.choice: only once a year, on the Day of Atonement
decisions.reason: Readable names the day the author is describing (Leviticus 16), so a new reader can see what event this is.

decisions.choice: parable (Literal), figure (Balanced), picture (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "parable" so the reader sees the word the Gospels use for Jesus's parables; Balanced and Readable say what it is here: a figure or picture.

decisions.choice: the time when God would set things right
alternatives: the time of setting things right
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who sets things right, as the context implies (9:11, 8:8).

decisions.choice: hacer perfecto (Literal, Balanced), queden completos (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled Hebrews wording: "hacer perfecto" at Literal and Balanced, and at Readable the plainer "completo", as the English Readable says "complete". The worshiper, not the conscience, is the object, as in the Greek; "en su conciencia" says in what respect.

decisions.choice: sigue en pie (Literal), conserve su lugar (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Spanish "sigue en pie" is a natural way to say that something still has standing; Balanced and Readable say it keeps its place, as the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: kumkamilisha (every level)
decisions.reason: Swahili "kukamilisha" means both to make perfect and to bring to completion, so it carries the English Literal "perfect" and the Readable "complete" at once. It is kept at every level as the Hebrews term.

decisions.choice: mfano (Literal), kielelezo (Balanced), picha (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Mfano" is the word for Jesus's parables in Swahili and also means an example, so Literal keeps it as the English keeps "parable". Balanced says "kielelezo" (a figure or model) and Readable "picha" (a picture), as the English says "figure" and "picture".

decisions.choice: le jour du Grand Pardon
decisions.reason: Readable names the day, as the English Readable does. "Le jour du Grand Pardon" is the usual French name and says plainly what the day was for; "le jour des Expiations" is the older Bible name and "Yom Kippour" the Hebrew one.

decisions.choice: ablutions (Literal, Balanced), lavages (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the one from which "baptême" comes, but here it means the ritual washings of the law, as the meaning decision says. "Baptêmes" would make French readers think of Christian baptism, so Literal and Balanced say "ablutions", the word for ritual washing, and Readable says plainly "lavages".

source.text: Χριστὸς δὲ παραγενόμενος ἀρχιερεὺς τῶν γενομένων ἀγαθῶν διὰ τῆς μείζονος καὶ τελειοτέρας σκηνῆς οὐ χειροποιήτου, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν οὐ ταύτης τῆς κτίσεως, οὐδὲ δι’ αἵματος τράγων καὶ μόσχων διὰ δὲ τοῦ ἰδίου αἵματος, εἰσῆλθεν ἐφάπαξ εἰς τὰ ἅγια, αἰωνίαν λύτρωσιν εὑράμενος.

records.literal_gloss: Christ but having come [as] high priest of the having come good things, through the greater and more perfect tent not made with hands, that is, not of this the creation, \v 12 nor through blood of goats and calves, through but the own blood, entered once for all into the holy [place], eternal redemption having obtained.

en.L: But {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, having come [as] high priest of the good things that have come, through the greater and more perfect tent not made with hands, that is, not of this creation, \v 12 and not through [the] blood of goats and calves but through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own blood, entered once for all into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption.
en.B: But {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} came as high priest of the good things that have now come. Through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, one not made by hands and not belonging to this creation, \v 12 and by means not of the blood of goats and calves but of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own blood, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} entered the sanctuary once for all and obtained an eternal redemption.
en.R: But {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} has come as high priest of the good things that are already here. He went through a greater and more perfect sacred tent. No human hands made it; it is not part of this created world. \v 12 He did not bring the blood of goats and calves. He brought {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own blood, and with it {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} entered the true Most Holy Place once for all time. There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} won eternal redemption, a freedom that lasts forever.

es.L: Pero {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, habiéndose presentado [como] sumo sacerdote de los bienes que han llegado, a través de la tienda mayor y más perfecta, no hecha por manos, es decir, no de esta creación, \v 12 y no por medio de [la] sangre de machos cabríos y de becerros, sino por medio de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia sangre, entró una vez para siempre en el lugar santo, habiendo obtenido redención eterna.
es.B: Pero {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} vino como sumo sacerdote de los bienes que ya han llegado. A través del tabernáculo mayor y más perfecto, no hecho por manos ni perteneciente a esta creación, \v 12 y no por medio de la sangre de machos cabríos y becerros, sino de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia sangre, entró en el santuario una vez para siempre y obtuvo una redención eterna.
es.R: Pero {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} ha venido como sumo sacerdote de los bienes que ya están aquí. Pasó por una tienda sagrada mayor y más perfecta. Ninguna mano humana la hizo; no es parte de este mundo creado. \v 12 No llevó la sangre de machos cabríos ni de becerros. Llevó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia sangre, y con ella entró en el verdadero Lugar Santísimo una sola vez y para siempre. Allí obtuvo la redención eterna, una libertad que dura para siempre.

fr.L: Mais {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, venu [comme] grand prêtre des biens qui sont arrivés, à travers la tente plus grande et plus parfaite, non faite par des mains, c’est-à-dire pas de cette création, \v 12 et non par [le] sang de boucs et de veaux, mais par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre sang, est entré une fois pour toutes dans le lieu saint, ayant obtenu une rédemption éternelle.
fr.B: Mais {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} est venu comme grand prêtre des biens désormais arrivés. À travers le tabernacle plus grand et plus parfait, qui n’est pas fait par des mains humaines et n’appartient pas à cette création, \v 12 et au moyen non du sang des boucs et des veaux mais de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre sang, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est entré une fois pour toutes dans le sanctuaire et a obtenu une rédemption éternelle.
fr.R: Mais {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} est venu comme grand prêtre des biens qui sont déjà là. Il est passé par une tente sacrée plus grande et plus parfaite. Aucune main humaine ne l’a faite ; elle ne fait pas partie de ce monde créé. \v 12 Il n’a pas apporté le sang de boucs et de veaux. Il a apporté {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre sang, et avec ce sang {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est entré une fois pour toutes dans le vrai Lieu très saint. Là, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a obtenu une rédemption éternelle, une libération qui dure pour toujours.

sw.L: Lakini {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, alipokuja [akiwa] kuhani mkuu wa mambo mema yaliyokwisha kuja, kupitia hema iliyo kuu zaidi na kamilifu zaidi, isiyotengenezwa kwa mikono, yaani, isiyo ya uumbaji huu, \v 12 wala si kwa njia ya damu ya mbuzi na ya ndama, bali kwa njia ya damu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}, aliingia mara moja kwa daima katika mahali patakatifu, akiwa amepata ukombozi wa milele.
sw.B: Lakini {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alikuja akiwa kuhani mkuu wa mambo mema ambayo sasa yamekwisha kuja. Kupitia hema iliyo kuu zaidi na kamilifu zaidi, isiyotengenezwa kwa mikono wala si ya uumbaji huu, \v 12 na si kwa damu ya mbuzi na ndama bali kwa damu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}, aliingia mahali patakatifu mara moja kwa daima, akapata ukombozi wa milele.
sw.R: Lakini {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} amekuja akiwa kuhani mkuu wa mambo mema ambayo tayari yako hapa. Alipita katika hema takatifu iliyo kuu zaidi na kamilifu zaidi. Hakuna mikono ya binadamu iliyoitengeneza; si sehemu ya ulimwengu huu ulioumbwa. \v 12 Hakuleta damu ya mbuzi na ndama. Alileta damu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}, na kwa damu hiyo aliingia Patakatifu pa Patakatifu halisi mara moja kwa nyakati zote. Huko alipata ukombozi wa milele, uhuru unaodumu milele.

decisions.choice: the good things that have come
alternatives: the good things that are to come
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads γενομένων, "that have come", found in some of the earliest manuscripts (among them P46 and Codex Vaticanus). Many other manuscripts, including Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus and the later majority, read "that are to come", the wording of 10:1, which a copyist may have echoed here. The two readings differ only in viewpoint: the good things have arrived with Christ, yet are still awaited in full. Reviewers must check this note against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: through the greater and more perfect tent: the true tent of heaven (8:2), through which Christ passed into God's presence
decisions.reason: The author has called the heavenly sanctuary "the true tent, which the Lord set up, not a human being" (8:2), and in 9:24 says Christ entered "heaven itself". So "through" most likely means passing through the heavenly tent, as the high priest passed through the outer room to reach the inner one (compare 4:14, "passed through the heavens"). Some read the tent as Christ's body, since 10:20 speaks of his flesh as a curtain.

decisions.choice: through his own blood: by means of his own blood, the offering that gives entry
alternatives: carrying his own blood into heaven as a substance
decisions.reason: διὰ with blood means by means of, as the high priest entered "not without blood" (9:7). The author does not describe what happened in heaven in physical terms; the point is that Christ's own death, not an animal's, is the offering that opens the way.

decisions.choice: once for all: once, never to be repeated
decisions.reason: ἐφάπαξ means once and for all time, in contrast to the high priest's yearly entry (9:7, 9:25). The author repeats it in 7:27 and 10:10.

decisions.choice: eternal redemption: release bought at a price, valid forever
decisions.reason: λύτρωσιν is setting free by paying a price, as captives or slaves were redeemed. It is eternal because Christ's sacrifice is never repeated. The aorist participle εὑράμενος describes what his entry achieved.

decisions.choice: eternal redemption, a freedom that lasts forever
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "eternal redemption" and adds a plain explanation of the word.

decisions.choice: the true Most Holy Place
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the place Christ entered is the true inner sanctuary that the earthly one copied (9:24).

decisions.choice: machos cabríos
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the male goat of the sin offering, so Spanish says "machos cabríos" here and in 9:13 rather than the general "cabras".

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns ("yake", "mwenyewe")
decisions.reason: Swahili marks "he" inside the verb ("aliingia", "alipata"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only where Swahili has a free pronoun. This chapter therefore has fewer spans than the English.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} where the Greek has no article; le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} (Literal) where it has one
decisions.reason: French says "Christ" without an article as a name but needs one before "Messie", so where the Greek has the bare word (9:11, 9:24) the article goes inside the span. Where the Greek has the article (9:14, 9:28) Literal keeps it outside the span, as in John.

source.text: εἰ γὰρ τὸ αἷμα τράγων καὶ ταύρων καὶ σποδὸς δαμάλεως ῥαντίζουσα τοὺς κεκοινωμένους ἁγιάζει πρὸς τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς καθαρότητα, πόσῳ μᾶλλον τὸ αἷμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὃς διὰ πνεύματος αἰωνίου ἑαυτὸν προσήνεγκεν ἄμωμον τῷ θεῷ, καθαριεῖ τὴν συνείδησιν ἡμῶν ἀπὸ νεκρῶν ἔργων εἰς τὸ λατρεύειν θεῷ ζῶντι.

records.literal_gloss: If for the blood of goats and of bulls and ashes of a heifer sprinkling the [ones] having been defiled sanctifies for the of the flesh cleanness, \v 14 by how much more the blood of the Christ, who through spirit eternal himself offered unblemished to the God, will cleanse the conscience of us from dead works for the to serve God living.

en.L: For if the blood of goats and bulls and [the] ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled sanctifies for the cleanness of the flesh, \v 14 how much more will the blood of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, who through [the] eternal Spirit offered {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve [the] living God!
en.B: For if the blood of goats and bulls, and a heifer's ashes sprinkled on people who have become defiled, make them holy so that they are clean in body, \v 14 how much more will the blood of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} wash our conscience clean of dead works, so that we may worship the living God! Through the eternal Spirit {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} offered {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to God, a sacrifice without flaw.
en.R: The blood of goats and bulls is sprinkled on people who are unclean, and so are the ashes of a young cow. If these things make people holy, so that their bodies are clean, \v 14 then the blood of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} will do much more! Through the eternal Spirit, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} offered {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to God as a sacrifice with no flaw. His blood will wash our conscience clean from the deeds that lead to death, so that we can serve the living God.

es.L: Porque si la sangre de machos cabríos y de toros, y [la] ceniza de una novilla rociada sobre los que se han contaminado, santifica para la pureza de la carne, \v 14 ¡cuánto más la sangre del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, quien mediante [el] Espíritu eterno se ofreció a {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}} sin mancha a Dios, limpiará nuestra conciencia de obras muertas para servir [al] Dios vivo!
es.B: Porque si la sangre de machos cabríos y de toros, y la ceniza de una novilla rociada sobre los que se han contaminado, los santifica de modo que quedan limpios en el cuerpo, \v 14 ¡cuánto más la sangre {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} lavará nuestra conciencia de obras muertas, para que rindamos culto al Dios vivo! Mediante el Espíritu eterno, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se ofreció a {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}} a Dios, como sacrificio sin defecto.
es.R: La sangre de machos cabríos y de toros se rocía sobre las personas impuras, y también la ceniza de una vaca joven. Si estas cosas hacen santas a las personas, de modo que su cuerpo queda limpio, \v 14 ¡entonces la sangre {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} hará mucho más! Mediante el Espíritu eterno, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se ofreció a {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}} a Dios como sacrificio sin ningún defecto. Su sangre lavará nuestra conciencia de las acciones que llevan a la muerte, para que podamos servir al Dios vivo.

fr.L: Car si le sang des boucs et des taureaux, et [la] cendre d’une génisse dont on asperge ceux qui ont été souillés, sanctifient pour la pureté de la chair, \v 14 combien plus le sang du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, qui par [l’]Esprit éternel s’est offert {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} sans défaut à Dieu, purifiera-t-il notre conscience des œuvres mortes pour servir [le] Dieu vivant !
fr.B: Car si le sang des boucs et des taureaux, et la cendre d’une génisse répandue sur ceux qui sont devenus impurs, les sanctifient de sorte qu’ils sont purs dans leur corps, \v 14 combien plus le sang du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} lavera-t-il notre conscience des œuvres mortes, pour que nous rendions un culte au Dieu vivant ! Par l’Esprit éternel, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est offert {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} à Dieu, sacrifice sans défaut.
fr.R: On asperge les personnes impures avec le sang de boucs et de taureaux, et aussi avec la cendre d’une jeune vache. Si ces choses rendent les gens saints, si bien que leur corps est pur, \v 14 alors le sang du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} fera bien plus encore ! Par l’Esprit éternel, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est offert {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} à Dieu, comme un sacrifice sans aucun défaut. Son sang lavera notre conscience des actes qui mènent à la mort, pour que nous puissions servir le Dieu vivant.

sw.L: Kwa maana ikiwa damu ya mbuzi na ya mafahali, na majivu ya mtamba yanayowanyunyizia waliotiwa unajisi, hutakasa hata kuleta usafi wa mwili, \v 14 kwa kiasi gani zaidi damu ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ambaye kwa Roho wa milele alijitoa {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} bila dosari kwa Mungu, itaisafisha dhamiri yetu kutoka matendo yaliyokufa ili kumtumikia Mungu aliye hai!
sw.B: Kwa maana ikiwa damu ya mbuzi na mafahali, na majivu ya mtamba yanayonyunyizwa juu ya watu waliotiwa unajisi, huwatakasa hata wawe safi kimwili, \v 14 basi ni zaidi sana jinsi damu ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} itakavyoiosha dhamiri yetu iwe safi mbali na matendo yaliyokufa, ili tupate kumwabudu Mungu aliye hai! Kwa Roho wa milele alijitoa {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} kwa Mungu, dhabihu isiyo na dosari.
sw.R: Damu ya mbuzi na mafahali hunyunyizwa juu ya watu walio najisi, na vivyo hivyo majivu ya ng'ombe mchanga wa kike. Ikiwa vitu hivyo huwatakasa watu, hata miili yao ikawa safi, \v 14 basi damu ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} itafanya mengi zaidi sana! Kwa Roho wa milele, alijitoa {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} kwa Mungu kama dhabihu isiyo na dosari yoyote. Damu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} itaiosha dhamiri yetu iwe safi, mbali na matendo yanayoleta mauti, ili tuweze kumtumikia Mungu aliye hai.

decisions.choice: goats and bulls; the ashes of a heifer: the Day of Atonement and the red heifer
decisions.reason: A bull and a goat were sacrificed on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:11, 16:15). The ashes of a red heifer, mixed with water, were sprinkled on anyone made unclean by touching a dead body (Numbers 19:1-22). Both rites cleansed from defilement that barred a person from worship.

decisions.choice: sanctifies for the cleanness of the flesh: makes a person ritually fit for worship again, an outward cleanness
decisions.reason: ἁγιάζει here means to set apart as fit for God. What these rites gave was the cleanness of the σαρκὸς, the outward, bodily purity the law required (9:10). The contrast with verse 14 is between that and the cleansing of the conscience.

decisions.choice: through the eternal Spirit: through the Holy Spirit
alternatives: through his own eternal spirit, his divine nature
through an eternal, spiritual power (his indestructible life, 7:16)
decisions.reason: There is no article, so the phrase could mean Christ's own eternal spirit. But Hebrews speaks often of the Holy Spirit (2:4; 6:4; 9:8; 10:15, 10:29), and the Spirit rested on the Servant of the Lord who would give his life (Isaiah 42:1; 53:10-12). The word "eternal" sets this offering apart from offerings that had to be repeated.

decisions.choice: unblemished: without defect, as a sacrificial animal had to be
decisions.reason: ἄμωμον is the word the law uses for animals fit for sacrifice (Leviticus 22:21; Numbers 19:2). Applied to Christ it means he was without sin (4:15; 7:26).

decisions.choice: dead works: deeds that belong to death and defile, keeping a person from worship
alternatives: works of the law that cannot give life
decisions.reason: The phrase also appears at 6:1. Here it follows the ashes of the heifer, which cleansed from contact with a dead body (Numbers 19:11-13). As a corpse made a person unclean, so these works defile the conscience; Christ's blood cleanses it so that the worshiper may serve the living God.

decisions.choice: serve: worship and serve God as a priest serves
decisions.reason: λατρεύω is the verb for worship and priestly service, the same family as "worship" in 9:1, 9:6 and "worshiper" in 9:9. What only priests did in the earthly tent, all whose conscience is cleansed may now do.

decisions.choice: sanctifies (Literal), make holy (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal says "sanctify" for this verb throughout Hebrews; Balanced and Readable say "make holy".

decisions.choice: a separate sentence after the main clause
alternatives: a relative clause in the middle of the sentence, as in the Greek
decisions.reason: Balanced moves the relative clause about Christ's offering after the main question so the long sentence can be followed when read aloud. Readable does the same.

decisions.choice: the deeds that lead to death
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase "dead works" in plain words, following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: santifica (Literal, Balanced), hacen santas (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled Hebrews wording: "santificar" at Literal and Balanced, "hacer santo" at Readable. The English Balanced says "make holy"; Spanish "santificar" is an everyday word and keeps the link with the rest of Hebrews.

decisions.choice: a separate sentence after the main clause
decisions.reason: As in the English Balanced: the relative clause about Christ's self-offering becomes its own sentence after the exclamation, so the comparison "cuánto más" stays clear.

decisions.choice: kutakasa (every level)
decisions.reason: "Kutakasa" is the Hebrews term for sanctify and already says "make holy" in ordinary words, so Swahili keeps it at every level where the English moves from "sanctify" to "make holy". It is kept apart from "kusafisha" and "kuosha" (cleanse) in verse 14.

decisions.choice: sanctifier (Literal, Balanced), rendre saint (Readable)
alternatives: rendre saint at Balanced, as the English "make holy"
decisions.reason: "Sanctifier" is the French word for this verb through Hebrews at Literal and Balanced; it is ordinary church French and keeps the link with 2:11, 10:10 and 13:12. Readable says "rendre saint". This departs from the English Balanced, which says "make holy"; the meaning is the same.

source.text: Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο διαθήκης καινῆς μεσίτης ἐστίν, ὅπως θανάτου γενομένου εἰς ἀπολύτρωσιν τῶν ἐπὶ τῇ πρώτῃ διαθήκῃ παραβάσεων τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν λάβωσιν οἱ κεκλημένοι τῆς αἰωνίου κληρονομίας.

records.literal_gloss: And because of this of a covenant new mediator he is, so that, death having occurred for redemption of the under the first covenant transgressions, the promise may receive the [ones] having been called of the eternal inheritance.

en.L: And because of this {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is mediator of a new covenant, so that, a death having occurred for redemption from the transgressions under the first covenant, those who have been called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
en.B: This is why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} mediates a new covenant: a death has taken place to set people free from the offenses committed under the first covenant, and so those who are called may receive what was promised, the eternal inheritance.
en.R: That is why {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} brings a new covenant between God and people. He died to set people free from the wrong things they did under the first covenant. Now those whom God has called can receive the eternal inheritance {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised them.

es.L: Y por esto es mediador de un pacto nuevo, para que, habiendo ocurrido una muerte para redención de las transgresiones [cometidas] bajo el primer pacto, los que han sido llamados reciban la promesa de la herencia eterna.
es.B: Por eso es mediador de un pacto nuevo: ha tenido lugar una muerte que libera a las personas de las faltas cometidas bajo el primer pacto, y así los que son llamados pueden recibir lo prometido, la herencia eterna.
es.R: Por eso {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} trae un pacto nuevo entre Dios y las personas. Murió para liberar a la gente de las cosas malas que hicieron bajo el primer pacto. Ahora los que Dios ha llamado pueden recibir la herencia eterna que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les prometió.

fr.L: Et c’est pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est médiateur d’une alliance nouvelle, afin que, une mort ayant eu lieu pour la rédemption des transgressions [commises] sous la première alliance, ceux qui ont été appelés reçoivent la promesse de l’héritage éternel.
fr.B: Voilà pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est le médiateur d’une alliance nouvelle : une mort a eu lieu pour libérer des fautes commises sous la première alliance, afin que ceux qui sont appelés reçoivent ce qui était promis, l’héritage éternel.
fr.R: C’est pour cela que {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} apporte une nouvelle alliance entre Dieu et les humains. Il est mort pour libérer les gens du mal qu’ils avaient fait sous la première alliance. Maintenant, ceux que Dieu a appelés peuvent recevoir l’héritage éternel qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a promis.

sw.L: Na kwa sababu hii {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mpatanishi wa agano jipya, ili kwamba, kifo kikiwa kimetokea kwa ukombozi kutoka kwa makosa yaliyokuwa chini ya agano la kwanza, wale walioitwa wapokee ahadi ya urithi wa milele.
sw.B: Ndiyo sababu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mpatanishi wa agano jipya: kifo kimetokea ili kuwaweka watu huru kutoka kwa makosa yaliyotendwa chini ya agano la kwanza, na hivyo walioitwa wapate kupokea kile kilichoahidiwa, yaani, urithi wa milele.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} analeta agano jipya kati ya Mungu na watu. Alikufa ili kuwaweka watu huru kutoka kwa makosa waliyoyatenda chini ya agano la kwanza. Sasa wale ambao Mungu amewaita wanaweza kupokea urithi wa milele ambao aliwaahidi.

decisions.choice: mediator of a new covenant: the one through whom the new covenant is made and put into effect
decisions.reason: The author has quoted the new covenant promise of Jeremiah 31:31-34 (8:8-12) and called Christ its mediator (8:6; again 12:24). Moses was the mediator of the first covenant (Galatians 3:19); Christ mediates the new one by his own death.

decisions.choice: a death for redemption from transgressions under the first covenant: Christ's death frees even those who broke the first covenant
alternatives: only sins committed after Christ's coming
decisions.reason: ἀπολύτρωσιν is release by payment, as in 9:12. The first covenant's sacrifices could not take away sins (10:4), so Christ's death reaches back to the wrongs done under it (compare 11:39-40).

decisions.choice: the promise of the eternal inheritance: the inheritance God promised, which lasts forever
decisions.reason: The inheritance is the promised rest and the city to come (4:1; 11:10, 11:16; 13:14). The word "inheritance" prepares for the next verses, where the author speaks of a will that takes effect at a death.

decisions.choice: Christ, the Messiah (for "he")
decisions.reason: Readable names Christ (the Messiah) as the subject, since this record begins a new paragraph. It also says what a mediator does (brings a covenant between God and people).

decisions.choice: those whom God has called ... he promised them
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who calls and promises, as the passive verb implies.

decisions.choice: es mediador, with no subject pronoun
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves out the subject pronoun, so the English "he" has no counterpart at Literal and Balanced; the verb shows the subject, Christ, from 9:11-14.

decisions.choice: mpatanishi
decisions.reason: "Mpatanishi" is one who brings two parties together, which is what a mediator of a covenant does (see the meaning decision). "Mjumbe" is only a messenger. Readable says what he does instead of naming the office, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ὅπου γὰρ διαθήκη, θάνατον ἀνάγκη φέρεσθαι τοῦ διαθεμένου·

records.literal_gloss: Where for [there is] a will, death [is] necessary to be brought forward of the [one] having made [it];

en.L: For where [there is] a will, [the] death of the one who made [it] must be established.
en.B: A will, after all, requires proof that the one who made it has died.
en.R: Think about a will. It must first be shown that the person who made it has died.

es.L: Porque donde [hay] un testamento, es necesario que se compruebe [la] muerte del que lo hizo.
es.B: Un testamento, al fin y al cabo, requiere la prueba de que el testador ha muerto.
es.R: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en un testamento. Primero hay que mostrar que la persona que lo hizo ha muerto.

fr.L: Car là où [il y a] un testament, il est nécessaire que soit établie la mort de celui qui [l’]a fait.
fr.B: Un testament, en effet, exige la preuve que son auteur est mort.
fr.R: Pensez à un testament. Il faut d’abord montrer que la personne qui l’a fait est morte.

sw.L: Kwa maana palipo na wasia, ni lazima kifo cha yule aliyeufanya kithibitishwe.
sw.B: Wasia, kwa kweli, unahitaji uthibitisho kwamba yule aliyeuandika amekufa.
sw.R: Fikirini kuhusu wasia. Kwanza lazima ionyeshwe kwamba mtu aliyeuandika amekwisha kufa.

decisions.choice: will: a person's last testament, which takes effect at death; the author plays on the double sense of the word he uses for covenant
alternatives: covenant, which was confirmed over slain animals that stood for the one making it
decisions.reason: διαθήκη is the word translated "covenant" in 9:15 and 9:18 and through Hebrews. In ordinary Greek of the time its common meaning was a will, a person's last testament, and the verb διαθεμένου is the usual word for making one. The author has just spoken of an inheritance (9:15), and in 9:16-17 he says the διαθήκη needs the death of the one who made it and has no force while that person lives. That describes a will exactly, so he seems to be using the word's other sense to make his point: Christ's death puts into effect what God has promised. On the other side, a covenant in the Old Testament was confirmed over the bodies of slain animals (Genesis 15:9-18; Jeremiah 34:18-20), verse 17 says "over dead [ones]" in the plural, and verses 15 and 18 speak of covenants. On that reading, the death required is the death of the sacrifice that represents the one making the covenant. Both readings have weight.

decisions.choice: must be established: the death has to be proven or put on record
decisions.reason: φέρεσθαι literally means "to be brought". In legal use it can mean to be brought forward as evidence, so the sense is that the death must be shown to have happened before the will can be acted on.

decisions.choice: will
decisions.reason: All three levels say "will" in 9:16-17, following the meaning decision, so the reader sees the shift from "covenant" in 9:15 at every level; the footnote gives "covenant". "Testament" is an older word that most readers now know only from the names of the Old and New Testaments.

decisions.choice: testamento
decisions.reason: Here the word for covenant has its everyday sense of a last will, which takes effect at death (see the meaning decision). Spanish "testamento" says that, and since Spanish readers know the word also from the names of the two Testaments, it keeps something of the author's play on the two senses. Spanish returns to "pacto" at 9:18.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: As through the New Testament: each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting, ustedes (the default) or vosotros. Here it is the Readable invitation to the reader, and again in the quotation at 9:20.

decisions.choice: wasia
decisions.reason: Here the word for covenant has its everyday sense of a last will, which takes effect at death (see the meaning decision). Swahili "wasia" is that word, and it is used in 9:16-17 only, so that the reader sees the shift from "agano" in 9:15 at every level; the footnote gives "agano".

decisions.choice: testament (9:16-17 only)
decisions.reason: Following the meaning decision, French says "testament", the ordinary word for a last will, in 9:16-17 at every level, so that the shift from "alliance" in 9:15 is visible; the footnote gives "alliance". Unlike English "testament", the French word is in everyday use. French readers also know it from "Ancien" and "Nouveau Testament", which echoes the author's play on the one Greek word.

source.text: διαθήκη γὰρ ἐπὶ νεκροῖς βεβαία, ἐπεὶ μήποτε ἰσχύει ὅτε ζῇ ὁ διαθέμενος.

records.literal_gloss: A will for over dead [ones] [is] valid, since never it is in force when lives the [one] having made [it].

en.L: For a will [is] valid over dead [people], since it is never in force while the one who made [it] is living.
en.B: For it is when someone has died that a will becomes binding; it has no force at all as long as its maker is alive.
en.R: A will only becomes valid after someone dies. It does nothing while the person who made it is still living.

es.L: Porque un testamento [es] válido sobre muertos, puesto que nunca tiene fuerza mientras vive el que lo hizo.
es.B: Pues un testamento entra en vigor cuando alguien ha muerto; no tiene ninguna fuerza mientras vive el testador.
es.R: Un testamento solo tiene validez después de que alguien muere. No sirve de nada mientras la persona que lo hizo sigue viva.

fr.L: Car un testament [est] valide sur des morts, puisqu’il n’est jamais en vigueur tant que vit celui qui [l’]a fait.
fr.B: C’est en effet quand quelqu’un est mort qu’un testament devient valable ; il n’a aucune force tant que son auteur est en vie.
fr.R: Un testament ne devient valable qu’après la mort de quelqu’un. Il ne sert à rien tant que la personne qui l’a fait est encore en vie.

sw.L: Kwa maana wasia [ni] halali juu ya waliokufa, kwa kuwa hauna nguvu kamwe wakati yule aliyeufanya angali hai.
sw.B: Kwa maana wasia huwa na nguvu ya kisheria pale mtu anapokwisha kufa; hauna nguvu yoyote maadamu aliyeuandika yu hai.
sw.R: Wasia huwa halali tu baada ya mtu kufa. Haufanyi kitu chochote wakati mtu aliyeuandika bado yu hai.

decisions.choice: will: as in 9:16, the word for covenant used in its sense of a last testament
alternatives: covenant, confirmed over the bodies of sacrificed animals
decisions.reason: See the decision on 9:16. The plural νεκροῖς, "over dead [ones]", fits the slain animals of a covenant rite as well as the death of a testator, which is why the reading "covenant" remains possible here.

decisions.choice: never: a firm denial
alternatives: a question: is it ever in force while the one who made it lives?
decisions.reason: μήποτε normally introduces a cautious or questioning clause, but here it most likely works as a strong "never". Read as a question expecting the answer no, the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: will
decisions.reason: The same English word as in 9:16, at every level.

decisions.choice: testamento
decisions.reason: As in 9:16: the word has its sense of a last will here.

decisions.choice: wasia
decisions.reason: As in 9:16: the word has its sense of a last will here.

source.text: ὅθεν οὐδὲ ἡ πρώτη χωρὶς αἵματος ἐγκεκαίνισται·

records.literal_gloss: Whence not even the first without blood has been inaugurated;

en.L: Therefore not even the first [covenant] has been inaugurated without blood.
en.B: This is why not even the first covenant was dedicated apart from blood.
en.R: That is why even the first covenant had to begin with blood.

es.L: Por lo cual ni siquiera el primer [pacto] ha sido inaugurado sin sangre.
es.B: Por eso ni siquiera el primer pacto fue consagrado sin sangre.
es.R: Por eso hasta el primer pacto tuvo que comenzar con sangre.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi même la première [alliance] n’a pas été inaugurée sans sang.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi la première alliance elle-même n’a pas été consacrée sans le sang.
fr.R: C’est pour cela que même la première alliance a dû commencer avec du sang.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo hata [agano] la kwanza halikuzinduliwa bila damu.
sw.B: Ndiyo sababu hata agano la kwanza halikuwekwa wakfu bila damu.
sw.R: Ndiyo maana hata agano la kwanza lilipaswa kuanza kwa damu.

decisions.choice: the first: the first covenant
decisions.reason: As in 9:1, the feminine πρώτη has no noun. After the illustration of a will (9:16-17), the author returns to the covenant at Sinai, which verses 19-20 describe.

decisions.choice: inaugurated: put into effect and dedicated at its start
decisions.reason: ἐγκεκαίνισται means to dedicate or open something new; the Greek Old Testament uses the related word for dedicating the temple (1 Kings 8:63). The same verb is used in 10:20 of the new way Christ opened.

decisions.choice: dedicated
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the plain word "dedicated"; Literal keeps "inaugurated"; Readable says the covenant had to "begin" with blood.

decisions.choice: pacto again
decisions.reason: From here the author speaks again of the covenant made at Sinai, so Spanish returns from "testamento" (9:16-17) to "pacto", supplied in brackets at Literal.

decisions.choice: agano again
decisions.reason: From here the author speaks again of the covenant made at Sinai, so Swahili returns from "wasia" (9:16-17) to "agano", supplied in brackets at Literal.

source.text: λαληθείσης γὰρ πάσης ἐντολῆς κατὰ τὸν νόμον ὑπὸ Μωϋσέως παντὶ τῷ λαῷ, λαβὼν τὸ αἷμα τῶν μόσχων μετὰ ὕδατος καὶ ἐρίου κοκκίνου καὶ ὑσσώπου αὐτό τε τὸ βιβλίον καὶ πάντα τὸν λαὸν ἐράντισεν, λέγων· Τοῦτο τὸ αἷμα τῆς διαθήκης ἧς ἐνετείλατο πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὁ θεός·

records.literal_gloss: Having been spoken for every commandment according to the law by Moses to all the people, having taken the blood of the calves with water and wool scarlet and hyssop, itself both the book and all the people he sprinkled, \v 20 saying, This [is] the blood of the covenant which commanded to you the God.

en.L: For when every commandment according to the law had been spoken by Moses to all the people, having taken the blood of the calves with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, he sprinkled both the book itself and all the people, \v 20 saying, "This [is] the blood of the covenant that God commanded to you."
en.B: Moses first spoke every command of the law to all the people. Then he took the calves' blood together with water, scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled the book itself and the whole people, \v 20 and said, "This is the blood of the covenant God has laid down for you."
en.R: First Moses told all the people every command in the law. Then he took the blood of the calves, along with water, red wool and branches of hyssop. He sprinkled the book of the law and all the people. \v 20 He said, "This is the blood of the covenant that God has set up for you by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} command."

es.L: Porque habiendo sido anunciado todo mandamiento conforme a la ley por Moisés a todo el pueblo, tomando la sangre de los becerros con agua y lana escarlata e hisopo, roció tanto el libro mismo como a todo el pueblo, \v 20 diciendo: «Esta [es] la sangre del pacto que Dios ordenó para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}».
es.B: Moisés primero proclamó a todo el pueblo cada mandamiento de la ley. Luego tomó la sangre de los becerros junto con agua, lana escarlata e hisopo, y roció el libro mismo y a todo el pueblo, \v 20 y dijo: «Esta es la sangre del pacto que Dios ha establecido para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}».
es.R: Primero Moisés dijo a todo el pueblo cada mandamiento de la ley. Después tomó la sangre de los becerros, junto con agua, lana roja y ramas de hisopo. Roció el libro de la ley y a todo el pueblo. \v 20 Dijo: «Esta es la sangre del pacto que Dios ha establecido para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mandato».

fr.L: Car après que chaque commandement selon la Loi eut été dit par Moïse à tout le peuple, ayant pris le sang des veaux avec de l’eau, de la laine écarlate et de l’hysope, il aspergea à la fois le livre lui-même et tout le peuple, \v 20 en disant : « Ceci [est] le sang de l’alliance que Dieu a commandée pour vous. »
fr.B: Moïse avait d’abord dit à tout le peuple chaque commandement de la Loi. Puis il prit le sang des veaux, avec de l’eau, de la laine écarlate et de l’hysope, et il aspergea le livre lui-même et tout le peuple, \v 20 en disant : « Ceci est le sang de l’alliance que Dieu a fixée pour vous. »
fr.R: Moïse a d’abord dit à tout le peuple chaque commandement de la Loi. Ensuite, il a pris le sang des veaux, avec de l’eau, de la laine rouge et des branches d’hysope. Il a aspergé le livre de la Loi et tout le peuple. \v 20 Il a dit : « Ceci est le sang de l’alliance que Dieu a établie pour vous par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} commandement. »

sw.L: Kwa maana kila amri kulingana na sheria ilipokwisha kunenwa na Musa kwa watu wote, alichukua damu ya ndama pamoja na maji na sufu nyekundu na hisopo, akanyunyiza kitabu chenyewe na watu wote, \v 20 akisema, "Hii [ni] damu ya agano ambalo Mungu aliamuru kwenu."
sw.B: Musa aliwatangazia watu wote kwanza kila amri ya sheria. Kisha akachukua damu ya ndama pamoja na maji, sufu nyekundu na hisopo, akanyunyiza kitabu chenyewe na watu wote, \v 20 akasema, "Hii ni damu ya agano ambalo Mungu ameliweka kwa ajili yenu."
sw.R: Kwanza Musa aliwaambia watu wote kila amri iliyo katika sheria. Kisha akachukua damu ya ndama, pamoja na maji, sufu nyekundu na matawi ya hisopo. Akanyunyiza kitabu cha sheria na watu wote. \v 20 Alisema, "Hii ni damu ya agano ambalo Mungu amewawekea kwa amri {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}."

decisions.choice: a quotation of Exodus 24:8
decisions.reason: At Sinai Moses read the book of the covenant to the people, sprinkled half the blood of the offerings on the altar and the rest on the people, and said, in the Greek of Exodus, "Look, the blood of the covenant that the Lord made with you" (Exodus 24:3-8).
